title: Key strategy calls were deferred to AI; the six students have not yet argued them through
problem: Key calls (lock the ten payments first, the $150k floor, the half split) began as AI council output, and the team's own doc says so. The team did act on them (1 Oct 'IPS content locked'; trades 6-8 Oct), but no record shows the students' own reasons, the options they rejected, or who argued what. The old 'team has not read the memos' line is from 28 Sep and is out of date. Without a student-owned reason for each core decision, the team cannot honestly explain its decision-making process (an Articulation requirement), and Wharton treats using AI ideas as your own as plagiarism unless cited.

title: Nobody owns the numbers: $294,453 vs $298,624 ladder cost on the same 15 Oct curve (reason and which to use)
problem: Two AI pipelines a day apart gave two ladder costs on the same 15 Oct curve, and no student owns the basis. The number sheet ($294,453, room $5,547) discounts each $50k to its 1 Jan payment date with forward rates. L08 ($298,624, room $1,376 or 4.7bp) prices the actual WInS holdings at their earlier maturity dates, with the early cash earning nothing and yields unchanged. Both sums are right on their own basis. Because the team's own trade notes say early proceeds wait in a short-term Treasury ETF, about $294.5k-$295k (room about $5k, 16-19bp) is the fair figure for what the plan costs. About $298.6k (4.7bp) is the cautious bound and the like-for-like check on the IBTR note's 0.2-point trigger. The '1 in 3' odds are fair on the market-rate basis; 45% applies only if early cash earns 0%.

verifier_note: The diagnosis is right; the recommendation is not. I re-ran calc/basis.py on the official 15 Oct par curve (caplet-latest/competition/official_market_data/daily-treasury-rates_2026-10.csv): payment-date zeros carried to 1 Jan 2027 = $294,453 (matches results.json); zeros at the WInS holding maturities with the early cash left idle = $297,841. L08's $298,624 is the same holding-date method on a 'yields unchanged' basis. The gap is about $3.4k from early cash earning nothing between each maturity and its payment, and about $0.8k from forward vs unchanged. But the team's own WInS notes say early proceeds wait in a short-term Treasury ETF (05_trading_note_reflection_wins_trading_notes.md, Feb-2037 and May-2038 notes). Cash that earns market short rates brings the holding-date cost back to roughly the payment-date figure. So about $294.5k-$295.3k (room about $4.7k-$5.5k, 16-19bp) is the right figure for 'what the ten payments cost' in the IPS and Final Report. $298.6k (room $1.4k, 4.7bp) is a conservative bound, and it is the like-for-like check for the IBTR note's 'about 0.2 percentage points' trigger, which was stated on that holding-date basis (22.7bp on 6 Oct). The '45%' top-up odds hold only on the 0%-cash basis; on market-rate bases the L08 verifier got about 28-33%, so '1 in 3' is fair.
